text_to_speech: Triangulum Galaxy in unrivalled detail The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope has captured the most detailed image yet of the Triangulum Galaxy. Hubble recorded 54 images of the galaxy, totalling a staggering 665 million pixels. Only three million light-years away, the image of the Triangulum Galaxy reveals 15 million individual stars! The Triangulum Galaxy is the third largest galaxy in the Local Group, after the Andromeda Galaxy and our Milky Way. It has no central bulge, or a bar connecting the centre to the spiral arms... ...but its gaseous central region harbours rapid star formation — at a rate of one solar mass every two years. Hubblecast is produced by ESA/Hubble at the European Southern Observatory in Germany. The Hubble mission is a project of international cooperation between NASA and ESA. Subtitles:ESA/Hubble. youtube_description:
The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope has captured the most detailed image yet of a the Triangulum Galaxy, a spiral galaxy located at a distance of only three million light-years. The image of our cosmic neighbour is the second largest image ever created with Hubble data.  
  
You can subscribe to the Hubblecasts in iTunes, receive future episodes on YouTube or follow us on Vimeo.  
   
Many other Hubblecast episodes are also available.  
   
Find out how to view and contribute subtitles for the Hubblecast in multiple languages, or translate this video on YouTube.

More information and download options: http://www.spacetelescope.org/videos/heic1901a/
